scope: The state layer of India's energy/natural-resources power map: (1) verification of the Union energy-related cabinet portfolios as of 2026-09-25 against the repo's 2026-07-25 cabinet.json; (2) Chief Ministers and ruling parties for the 20 resource states named in the brief (Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, J&K, Assam, West Bengal, Goa, Uttar Pradesh), with dates of any change of ruling party 2019-2026; (3) a handful of deeply-sourced state-level resource-allocation decisions (Khavda and Dholera land allocation in Gujarat, Odisha discom privatisation, the Parsa East & Kanta Basan coal MDO arrangement, the Nov-2024 US indictment's state-contract allegations, the Maharashtra 6,600 MW Adani bid-rigging allegation, Tamil Nadu's 2024 Pumped Storage Projects Policy, the 2015 MMDR auction reform); (4) a symmetry attempt on opposition-run states. Deliberately NOT covered, for lack of verifiable sources within this session's budget: state energy/mines minister names for any of the 20 states (only Chief Ministers are recorded), most state gencos/transcos/mining corporations beyond the handful directly tied to a claim below, and granular opposition-state equivalents to the Gujarat/Maharashtra/Chhattisgarh cases — these are logged as gaps/voids rather than asserted.

The Election Commission of India reportedly recommended Hemant Soren's disqualification in 2022 for allegedly extending a mining lease to himself while in office — a self-dealing allegation distinct from the later ED land-fraud case. The source hedges with 'reportedly'; this session could not verify the lease name, its date, or whether the Governor acted on the recommendation. Soren was not in fact disqualified and continued as CM through 2024 and beyond, which is itself evidence the recommendation was not acted upon (or was overtaken by his subsequent resignation/arrest on the separate land matter).

This session located no on-record Soren/JMM denial of the specific 2022 mining-lease disqualification recommendation (that is itself the weakness of claim states:c007, per the fleet contract's rule that an unanswered ask must be recorded). What is documented is the outcome: the recommendation was not acted upon and Soren continued in and returned to office. Flagged as a gap for a follow-up search of JMM/Soren statements from 2022.

The Enforcement Directorate accused Soren of involvement in forging land records to illegally acquire 8.5 acres in Ranchi; he resigned 2024-01-31 hours ahead of arrest, spent ~5 months in judicial custody, and was granted bail by the Jharkhand High Court on 2024-06-28, which found reasons to believe he was 'not guilty of the offence.' No chargesheet or trial-stage information was found in the source consulted — recorded as a gap. Current stage as best known: released on bail; case status beyond June 2024 not verified this session.

claims.lab: Khavda: Gujarat's own PSUs self-allocate 11,400 ha
claims.d: At the Khavda Renewable Energy Park (Gujarat), Gujarat's own PSUs — GSECL (6,650 ha, ~3,325 MW) and Gujarat Industries Power Co / GIPCL (4,750 ha, ~2,375 MW) — together hold 11,400 of the ~50,400 hectares allocated to named developers in the table cited (about 23%), roughly comparable to Adani Green's single largest private share.

benefit.how: Direct land allocation to state-owned generators for self-owned capacity, not to a private beneficiary.

claims.lab: Khavda land allocation to Adani Green (largest single private share)
claims.d: Adani Green Energy holds a 19,000-hectare zone (~9,500 MW notional) at the Khavda Hybrid Renewable Energy Park, the largest single developer allocation in the park (total footprint 72,600 ha; approved 2020-09-09, foundation stone 2020-12-15). This is the single largest allocation in the table cited, but non-Adani entities (NTPC, Sarjan Realities, GSECL, GIPCL, and a SECI-bid wind zone) together hold a clear majority of the remaining land.

benefit.how: Land allocation for the largest single private RE zone at Khavda; allocation mechanism (nomination vs. proportional allotment to existing pipeline capacity) not confirmed this session.

claims.d: NTPC (central PSU) holds a 9,500-hectare zone (~4,750 MW notional) at Khavda, the second-largest single allocation and larger than any other private developer besides Adani Green.
srcs: Wikipedia: Gujarat Hybrid Renewable Energy Park (Khavda)

benefit.how: Land allocation to a central PSU for self-owned generation capacity.

claims.d: At Khavda, Adani Green's 19,000 ha is the single largest allocation (~38% of the five named zones totalling ~49,400 ha in the source table), but NTPC (central PSU, 9,500 ha) plus Gujarat's own GSECL/GIPCL (11,400 ha) plus Sarjan Realities (9,500 ha) together hold ~62% — a majority. A ~30 GW total target with a 23,000-hectare wind zone additionally reserved for SECI competitive bidding (not nomination) further dilutes any single-developer dominance claim.
claims.innocentReading: Adani Green was already the country's largest utility-scale renewable IPP by pipeline capacity before Khavda was announced (2020); a proportionally large slice of a co-developed park is consistent with market share, and the presence of a central PSU (NTPC), the state's own gencos, and an SECI-run competitive wind-tender zone in the same park is evidence against a park-wide favouritism pattern, even though Adani's individual zone is the largest.

claims.lab: US DOJ/SEC indictment: alleged bribes tied to state solar contracts across 5 states
claims.d: On 2024-11-20/21, US federal prosecutors (EDNY) indicted Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and other executives on five counts, alleging over $250 million (~₹2,075 crore at ~₹83/USD, DOJ's own figure, not independently reconverted from a primary filing) in bribes to Indian officials to secure solar-linked energy contracts across five states/UTs: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jammu & Kashmir and Tamil Nadu; and alleged concealment of the scheme from US investors while raising $3bn in loans/bonds. This session could not open the DOJ press release itself (404) or identify which specific named officials, roles, or per-state amounts are alleged — recorded as a gap. As of 2026-05, DOJ was reported moving to drop the charges; as of 2026-09, a US District Judge ruled the charges cannot be dropped until DOJ complies with the court's instructions — i.e. the case remains open and contested, not resolved either way.

benefit.how: Alleged bribery to secure state solar-energy supply contracts; not proven, contested in ongoing US litigation.

claims.upgradeIf: A chargesheet/conviction, or DOJ's court-ordered compliance filing, specifies a state-by-state breakdown that can be independently verified against a primary document.
claims.killIf: DOJ succeeds in withdrawing the indictment and no successor proceeding (SEC civil case, Indian agency action) sustains the allegation.

claims.d: Adani Group has publicly and repeatedly denied the US indictment's allegations as baseless in press statements reported contemporaneously with the November 2024 indictment. This session could not open a primary or press source carrying the exact denial text (Reuters and Livemint URLs were blocked/unreachable; Wikipedia's Gautam Adani and Adani Group articles, which this session did open, do not quote a denial statement) — the specific wording and date are therefore recorded as a gap, not fabricated.

claims.lab: All five indicted states have since changed ruling party — but turnover is the norm, not a signal
claims.d: All five states/UTs named in the Nov-2024 indictment (Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jammu & Kashmir, Tamil Nadu) have had a change of ruling party since the alleged 2021-22 conduct: AP (YSRCP→TDP-NDA, 2024-06), Chhattisgarh (INC→BJP, 2023-12), Odisha (BJD→BJP, 2024-06), J&K (Governor's/UT rule→elected JKNC, 2024-10), Tamil Nadu (DMK→TVK, 2026-05).
claims.innocentReading: India's state election cycle is roughly five years and anti-incumbency is a well-documented, near-universal pattern independent of any particular scandal; three of the five flips (Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu) replaced the incumbent with a different party for reasons with no established link to this case (Tamil Nadu's flip, in particular, was to a first-time actor-led party, not to the BJP or to an anti-Adani platform), so 5-for-5 turnover is not itself evidence that voters punished — or even knew about — the alleged conduct.

claims.lab: MMDR 2015 — the base instrument for mining-lease auctions
claims.d: The 2015 MMDR amendment made competitive auction the default mechanism for new mineral concessions nationally, applicable to all states including the resource states surveyed here. Blocks allotted before 2015 (like PEKB, states:c019) or transferred under grandfathered captive arrangements are the explanatory 'boring' baseline against which any specific non-auction allocation should be read, rather than assumed anomalous.

narratives.claim: Adani Group systematically receives the largest or most favourable allocation whenever a BJP-run state government makes a major renewable-energy land or power-purchase decision.
narratives.strongestCase: Adani Green holds the single largest private zone at Khavda (19,000 of ~72,600 ha); Adani Mining is MDO for a major Hasdeo Arand coal block; Adani Power is reported to have won a large (6,600 MW) Maharashtra supply contract that the opposition called bid-rigged; and Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and (until 2026) Tamil Nadu — all named in the Nov-2024 US indictment's bribery allegations — cover a geographically wide footprint of state contracts.
narratives.strongestCounter: At Khavda itself, non-Adani entities (a central PSU, Gujarat's own gencos, and an SECI-run competitive wind-tender zone) hold a clear majority of allocated land; the PEKB coal block is owned by a Rajasthan state PSU under a pre-2015 MDO structure that predates the current BJP-Rajasthan government by a decade; the Odisha discom privatisation — the largest state power-sector divestiture in this file — went to Tata Power, not Adani, under a regional (BJD) government; and the 2024 US indictment itself remains an unproven allegation currently contested in US courts (DOJ sought to drop it in 2026-05; a judge blocked that in 2026-09), not an adjudicated fact.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A verified state-by-state MW/hectare/₹ tally across all 20 states with allocation mechanism (nomination vs. auction) recorded for every major RE/mining/discom decision 2019-2026, plus resolution of the US indictment (chargesheet detail, dismissal, plea, or trial verdict).

symmetryCheck: Applied the same 'who benefited, by what mechanism, denial, boring explanation' lens to a control with no prior theory attached: Odisha's 2019-20 discom privatisation to Tata Power, approved under the BJD government of Naveen Patnaik — a regional party allied with neither national bloc at the time — produced the same shape of finding (a large public asset transferred to a major private conglomerate at a fixed equity split, 51/49) as the BJP-state cases, undercutting a purely partisan reading. The reverse control — an opposition (INC/BRS/DMK)-run state making a comparably large nominated (non-auction) award to a major private group — could not be established within this session's budget: attempted fetches for a Karnataka (INC) JSW Energy pumped-storage MoU and a Telangana (INC, post-BRS) review of Greenko/pumped-storage deals both returned no content. Tamil Nadu's 2024 Pumped Storage Projects Policy, enacted under the outgoing DMK government, shows the same category of private-developer-facing mechanism existing in an opposition state, though this session could not identify a specific beneficiary under it. Net finding: the lens produces a genuine cross-party pattern (large state-to-private-capital transfers happen under BJP, BJD and, on the mechanism-only evidence available, DMK governments alike); it could not be extended to a like-for-like MW/₹-scale comparison in an opposition state within budget, which is recorded as a gap rather than papered over.
